plain: Destruction and damage, such as from war

webster.text: Spoil; ruin; waste; destruction by violence, either by men, beasts or physical causes; as the ravage of a lion; the ravages of fire or tempest; the ravages of an army.

example.quote: Besides their natural propensity to barbarity, they may be excited, by the gold of foreign enemies, to commit the most horrid ravages on your people.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 3, Virginia Convention, June 6, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
